findings.claim: Early-onset Alzheimer's disease is defined as onset below 65 years, not below 40; the 1% figure applies to autosomal-dominant familial disease.
findings.evidence: "early onset (ages below 40), inherited due to defective genes ... accounts to 1% of the cases"
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Early-onset (<65 y, ~5% of cases; familial autosomal-dominant APP/PSEN1/PSEN2 <1%); late-onset (>=65 y, sporadic, APOE e4 risk).

findings.claim: Memantine is licensed for moderate-to-severe Alzheimer's disease, alone or added to a cholinesterase inhibitor; it is not only an add-on for rapid progression.
findings.evidence: "NMDA-receptor antagonists are usually used as Add-on drug in case of Sever and rapid progression"
findings.source: NICE NG97 Dementia (2018, updated 2023)
findings.fix_hint: State the NICE sequence: AChEI for mild-moderate; memantine for severe, for AChEI intolerance, or added in moderate-severe.

findings.claim: The chapter omits the anti-amyloid monoclonal antibodies (lecanemab, donanemab) now approved for early Alzheimer's disease, and their ARIA risk.
findings.evidence: "Treatment available are: Cholinesterase inhibitors ... NMDA blockers"
findings.source: FDA approvals of lecanemab (2023) and donanemab (2024)
findings.fix_hint: Add a short 'Newer agents' paragraph: mechanism, eligibility (early AD, amyloid-positive), ARIA monitoring by MRI.

findings.claim: Cholinesterase-inhibitor safety lists bradycardia but omits syncope and heart-block risk, pulse review, caution in conduction disease or with other bradycardic drugs, and titration advice.
findings.evidence: "Adverse effects include: ... Bradycardia. Salivation and Urination. Diarrhea"
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Add: review pulse before and during treatment; caution in conduction disease and with beta-blockers or digoxin; start low and titrate; rivastigmine with food; patch reduces GI effects.

findings.claim: Positive symptoms are linked to mesolimbic dopamine excess; the mesocortical pathway is hypoactive in schizophrenia.
findings.evidence: "Dopamine increase in mesolimbic and mesocortical track is responsible for these abnormalities"
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Positive symptoms: mesolimbic hyperactivity. Negative and cognitive symptoms: mesocortical hypoactivity.

findings.claim: Negative symptoms are attributed to serotonin; the accepted model links them to mesocortical dopamine hypofunction (5-HT2A block helps indirectly).
findings.evidence: "Negative symptoms: Serotonin is responsible for these manifestations."
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Rewrite: negative symptoms reflect reduced dopamine in the mesocortical pathway; 5-HT2A antagonism by SGAs releases dopamine there.

findings.claim: Extrapyramidal effects are misclassified: acute dystonia is reversible; tardive dyskinesia (late, potentially irreversible) and drug-induced parkinsonism are missing.
findings.evidence: "Dystonia abnormal uncontrolled body motions (irreversible)"
findings.source: Whalen K. Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Pharmacology. 8th ed. Wolters Kluwer; 2023
findings.fix_hint: Table of EPS by time of onset: acute dystonia (hours-days; IM anticholinergic), parkinsonism (weeks), akathisia (days-weeks; propranolol), tardive dyskinesia (months-years; often irreversible; valbenazine).

findings.claim: The neuroleptic malignant syndrome description omits altered mental status, autonomic lability, raised creatine kinase/rhabdomyolysis and urgent management; convulsions are not a defining feature.
findings.evidence: "Hyperthermia ,Convulsion ,Muscle rigidity ,hypertension and sweating"
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: NMS: fever, lead-pipe rigidity, altered mental state, autonomic instability (labile or raised BP, tachycardia, sweating), raised CK. Management: stop the antipsychotic, cool, fluids, supportive care; dantrolene or bromocriptine in severe cases.

findings.claim: The text says FGAs treat only negative symptoms; FGAs mainly treat positive symptoms.
findings.evidence: "SGAs improve treatment of –ve and +ve symptoms when compared to FGAs that treat only –ve symptoms."
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Replace '–ve' with '+ve' for FGAs.

findings.claim: Metabolic effects of SGAs are attributed to 5-HT2A block; they are mainly due to H1 and 5-HT2C antagonism.
findings.evidence: "Weight gain, diabetes, and hyperclosterolima due to 5-HT2A block"
findings.source: Whalen K. Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Pharmacology. 8th ed. Wolters Kluwer; 2023
findings.fix_hint: Weight gain and metabolic syndrome: H1 and 5-HT2C block (highest with clozapine and olanzapine); monitor weight, glucose and lipids.

findings.claim: Clozapine agranulocytosis is called 'leukopenia, often fatal and common' with no monitoring protocol.
findings.evidence: "Leukopenia: often fatal and is common with Clozapine."
findings.source: Clozapine prescribing information (REMS) 2025
findings.fix_hint: Agranulocytosis ~1%; baseline ANC, weekly for 18 weeks, then every 2 weeks to 1 year, then monthly; also myocarditis, seizures, constipation.

findings.claim: The cariprazine paragraph mixes olanzapine into its sentence, so 'It has a low liability for metabolic effects' has an unclear subject.
findings.evidence: "Olanzapine and others are widely used ... It has a low liability for metabolic effects"
findings.source: editorial
findings.fix_hint: Make cariprazine the explicit subject; move the olanzapine sentence to the SGA comparison table.

findings.claim: The FGA section lists only chlorpromazine, haloperidol and droperidol; low- versus high-potency differences (sedation/antimuscarinic vs EPS) are not explained.
findings.evidence: "Phenothiazines class :Chlorpromazine ... Butyrophenones class : Haloperidol and Droperidol"
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Add a potency table: chlorpromazine, thioridazine (low); fluphenazine, haloperidol (high) with typical adverse-effect profile.

findings.claim: Non-ergot dopamine agonists (pramipexole, ropinirole, rotigotine) are not taught, although they are standard therapy and appear in the chapter's own MCQs; only bromocriptine is covered.
findings.evidence: "D2 agonists (ergot alkaloids)"
findings.source: NICE NG71 Parkinson's disease (2017)
findings.fix_hint: Add non-ergot agonists as the main agonist class; keep bromocriptine as a historical ergot example.

findings.claim: Levodopa's short half-life is attributed to hepatic decarboxylases; peripheral AADC (gut wall, blood vessels) and COMT are responsible, and on/off fluctuations reflect disease progression plus short half-life.
findings.evidence: "due to peripheral decarboxylation by hepatic decarboxylases and COMT"
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Say 'peripheral dopa decarboxylase (AADC)'. Separate wearing-off and on/off from peripheral metabolism.

findings.claim: Dark urine and sweat with levodopa come from oxidation of catecholamine metabolites (melanin-like pigments), not specifically homovanillic acid.
findings.evidence: "brownish urine and sweat due to secretion of homovanillic acid"
findings.source: Whalen K. Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Pharmacology. 8th ed. Wolters Kluwer; 2023
findings.fix_hint: State the effect as harmless discoloration and counsel the patient.

findings.claim: Pyridoxine is said to be contraindicated with levodopa; the interaction applies to levodopa alone and is abolished by carbidopa, which almost all patients take.
findings.evidence: "Pyridoxine(Vitamin B6) is contraindicated with Levodopa"
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Pyridoxine enhances peripheral decarboxylation of levodopa given alone; with carbidopa/levodopa it is not clinically relevant.

findings.claim: MAO-B inhibitor interactions (serotonin syndrome with SSRIs, SNRIs, pethidine, tramadol; loss of selectivity at high doses) are missing.
findings.evidence: "No cheese reaction."
findings.source: Whalen K. Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Pharmacology. 8th ed. Wolters Kluwer; 2023
findings.fix_hint: Add: selectivity is dose-dependent; avoid pethidine and serotonergic drugs.

findings.claim: Pulmonary fibrosis is called 'very specific to bromocriptine'; fibrotic reactions are an ergot-derivative class effect (also cardiac valvulopathy).
findings.evidence: "Pulmonary fibrosis very specific to bromocriptin."
findings.source: Ritter JM et al. Rang & Dale's Pharmacology. 10th ed. Elsevier; 2023
findings.fix_hint: Say 'ergot-derived agonists (bromocriptine, cabergoline) can cause pulmonary, retroperitoneal and valvular fibrosis'.

findings.claim: Levodopa adverse effects omit dyskinesias, impulse-control disorders (also with agonists) and the MAOI-A hypertensive crisis interaction.
findings.evidence: "Adverse effects: CNS related side effects: Nausea and Vomiting ..."
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Add dyskinesia (peak-dose), impulse-control disorders, and 'never with non-selective MAOIs'.

findings.claim: Psychotherapy is presented as first line for all depression; guidelines reserve psychotherapy alone for less severe depression and combine it with an antidepressant for moderate-severe depression.
findings.evidence: "Psychotherapy with our without medication is the first line treatment to depression."
findings.source: NICE NG222 Depression in adults (2022)
findings.fix_hint: Stratify by severity and shared decision: less severe - guided self-help or psychological therapy first, antidepressant only if preferred; more severe - CBT plus antidepressant, an antidepressant, or psychological therapy according to need and preference (NICE NG222 1.5-1.6).

findings.claim: MAO-B is said to be in brain only and metabolise dopamine only; MAO-B is also in platelets and liver, and MAO-A metabolises serotonin, noradrenaline and tyramine.
findings.evidence: "Type B in brain only and metabolizes dopamine only"
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Table: MAO-A substrates (5-HT, NA, tyramine; gut and liver); MAO-B (dopamine, phenylethylamine; brain, platelets).

findings.claim: Orthostatic hypotension and sedation are listed as effects of all antidepressants due to raised amines; they are due to alpha1 and H1 block (TCAs, trazodone, mirtazapine) and are rare with SSRIs.
findings.evidence: "The following adverse effects are common with all anti-depressants: Orthostatic (Postural) hypotension, due to overall increase of bio amines"
findings.source: Whalen K. Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Pharmacology. 8th ed. Wolters Kluwer; 2023
findings.fix_hint: Attribute each effect to its receptor: alpha1 (hypotension), H1 (sedation, weight gain), M (anticholinergic), 5-HT (GI, sexual).

findings.claim: Serotonin syndrome is described incompletely (no triad, no management).
findings.evidence: "Serotonin Syndrome (hyperthermia , arrhythmia and increased mortality rate)"
findings.source: Hunter criteria; Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Triad: mental-status change, autonomic instability, neuromuscular hyperactivity (clonus, hyperreflexia); stop drugs, supportive care, cyproheptadine.

findings.claim: Yogurt is given as the typical tyramine food; the high-risk foods are aged cheese, cured or fermented meats, soy sauce and tap beer.
findings.evidence: "Certain foods like yogurt contain tyramine"
findings.source: Whalen K. Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Pharmacology. 8th ed. Wolters Kluwer; 2023
findings.fix_hint: Replace the example with aged cheese and cured meats.

findings.claim: The MAOI combination warning gives no washout periods.
findings.evidence: "MAO inhibitors are contraindicated in combination with other antidepressants"
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Washout: 2 weeks after stopping an MAOI; 5 weeks after fluoxetine before starting an MAOI.

findings.claim: 'Nor-amitriptyline' is not a drug name; the drug is nortriptyline.
findings.evidence: "Nor-amitriptyline ."
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Use nortriptyline.

findings.claim: TCA sedation is attributed to atropine-like action; it is due to H1 antagonism.
findings.evidence: "CNS sedation (due to Atropine like action)."
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Sedation: H1 block.

findings.claim: Routine PPI prescribing for SSRI GI upset is not standard advice; take with food, start low; PPI is considered only with added bleeding risk (NSAIDs, anticoagulants).
findings.evidence: "GIT disturbance (prescribe PPI)"
findings.source: NICE NG222 (2022)
findings.fix_hint: Counsel to take with food; GI effects settle in 1-2 weeks; gastroprotection if combined with NSAIDs.

findings.claim: The mechanisms of mirtazapine and trazodone are wrong or incomplete: mirtazapine is mainly an alpha2 antagonist (also 5-HT2, 5-HT3 and H1 block); trazodone is a 5-HT2A antagonist and weak SERT inhibitor.
findings.evidence: "Mirtazapine blocks 5HT2C"
findings.source: Whalen K. Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Pharmacology. 8th ed. Wolters Kluwer; 2023
findings.fix_hint: Mirtazapine: alpha2 antagonist raising NA and 5-HT release; 5-HT2/5-HT3 and H1 block (sedation, weight gain). Trazodone: 5-HT2A antagonist, weak SERT inhibitor, alpha1 and H1 block (priapism, sedation).

findings.claim: The chapter never mentions the boxed warning for suicidality in children and young adults starting antidepressants.
findings.evidence: "SSRI are first line treatment in major depression due to their safety even in large doses"
findings.source: FDA boxed warning for antidepressants (2007)
findings.fix_hint: Add a Caution box: monitor for suicidal thoughts in patients under 25 during the first weeks and after dose changes.

findings.claim: SSRI withdrawal is described as an 'acute attack of depression'; it is a discontinuation syndrome (dizziness, paraesthesia, irritability), worst with paroxetine.
findings.evidence: "SSRIs must stopped gradually (over 4 weeks) to avoid Acute attack of Depression."
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Name discontinuation syndrome; taper over at least 4 weeks; fluoxetine least affected.

findings.claim: First-generation drugs are said to act mainly on the inhibitory pathway and second-generation on the excitatory pathway; phenytoin and carbamazepine block Na+ channels and several second-generation drugs enhance GABA. The generalisation is false.
findings.evidence: "They mainly act on the inhibitory pathway." / "They mainly act on the excitatory pathway."
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Classify by mechanism (Na+ channel, T-type Ca2+, GABA, SV2A, alpha2delta, glutamate) in one table.

findings.claim: Enzyme induction, megaloblastic anaemia and teratogenicity are said to be common to all first-generation drugs; valproate is an enzyme inhibitor and ethosuximide is not an inducer.
findings.evidence: "The following adverse effects are common with all 1st generation epileptic drugs: ... Liver (microsomal enzyme induction)"
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Group inducers (phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital) versus inhibitor (valproate); teratogenicity highest with valproate.

findings.claim: Carbamazepine safety omits SJS/TEN with HLA-B*1502, aplastic anaemia/agranulocytosis, and failure of hormonal contraception through induction.
findings.evidence: "Adverse effects: Increase ADH secretion ... auto-induction"
findings.source: Carbamazepine prescribing information (boxed warning)
findings.fix_hint: Add the boxed warnings and interactions (oral contraceptives, warfarin).

findings.claim: The chapter has no drug-of-choice table by seizure type and no status epilepticus algorithm.
findings.evidence: "Classification of Epilepsy ... Generalized Onset seizures"
findings.source: NICE NG217 Epilepsies (2022)
findings.fix_hint: Add a seizure-type table (focal: lamotrigine/levetiracetam; generalised tonic-clonic: valproate in males, lamotrigine/levetiracetam in women of child-bearing potential; absence: ethosuximide) and a status epilepticus box (benzodiazepine then second-line agent).

findings.claim: Valproate's haematological effect is thrombocytopenia (neutropenia is less typical), and the pregnancy rule is a pregnancy-prevention programme rather than an absolute prohibition.
findings.evidence: "Neutropenia ." / "Valproic acid is strictly prohibited in pregnancy"
findings.source: MHRA valproate safety measures (2024)
findings.fix_hint: Say thrombocytopenia; valproate must not be used in women of child-bearing potential unless the pregnancy prevention programme is met.

findings.claim: 'AMBA receptors' should be AMPA/kainate receptors.
findings.evidence: "Block AMBA receptors. (similar to NMDA receptor)"
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: AMPA/kainate glutamate receptors.

findings.claim: Gabapentin and pregabalin bind the alpha2delta subunit of voltage-gated Ca2+ channels, not 'P/Q calcium channels'.
findings.evidence: "Binding to pre-synaptic P/Q calcium channels"
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Bind alpha2delta-1 subunit of presynaptic voltage-gated Ca2+ channels, reducing glutamate release.

findings.claim: The valproate/pregnancy MCQ is printed twice.
findings.evidence: Lines 1831-1856 repeat at 1858-1883
findings.source: editorial
findings.fix_hint: Keep one copy.

findings.claim: The pathophysiology sentence is garbled and the absence-seizure mechanism ('during the day causing a sleep-like state') is unclear.
findings.evidence: "An imbalance between glutamate and which activates NMDA receptors"
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Absence seizures: T-type Ca2+ currents in thalamocortical relay neurons generate 3 Hz spike-and-wave discharges.

findings.claim: Baclofen is said to increase chloride influx; GABA-B is a G-protein-coupled receptor that opens K+ channels and reduces presynaptic Ca2+ influx.
findings.evidence: "hypothesized to cause An Increase chloride influx which causes nerve hyperpolarization"
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: GABA-B agonist: increases K+ conductance (hyperpolarisation) and reduces Ca2+ entry, lowering excitatory transmitter release in the spinal cord.

findings.claim: 'hydration derivative' should read 'hydantoin derivative'.
findings.evidence: "Dantrolene is a hydration derivative related to phenytoin"
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Hydantoin derivative.

findings.claim: The classification table says depolarising blockers cause hyperpolarisation; they cause persistent depolarisation.
findings.evidence: "by constant activation of the receptor which causes a state of hyperpolarization"
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Persistent depolarisation (phase I) followed by desensitisation (phase II).

findings.claim: Succinylcholine safety omits hyperkalaemia (burns, crush injury, denervation, myopathy), bradycardia, raised intra-ocular pressure and muscle pain.
findings.evidence: "Adverse effects : Malignant hyperthermia ... Apnea"
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Add hyperkalaemia with contraindications, bradycardia (atropine), myalgia, raised IOP and ICP.

findings.claim: Reversal covers only neostigmine; sugammadex, the selective reversal agent for rocuronium and vecuronium, is missing.
findings.evidence: "Their competitive action can be overcome by administration of small doses of cholinesterase inhibitors, such as neostigmine."
findings.source: Whalen K. Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Pharmacology. 8th ed. Wolters Kluwer; 2023
findings.fix_hint: Add sugammadex: encapsulates rocuronium/vecuronium; no muscarinic side effects.

findings.claim: 'These agents are safe with minimal side effects' ignores histamine release (atracurium, mivacurium), residual paralysis and awareness risk.
findings.evidence: "In general, these agents are safe with minimal side effects."
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: State the main adverse effects and the need for monitoring (train-of-four).

findings.claim: Benzodiazepine half-life classes are wrong: diazepam and clonazepam are long-acting (diazepam 20-80 h plus active nordiazepam); oxazepam is short-intermediate; lorazepam, used later, is missing.
findings.evidence: "intermediate acting BZ (t1/2 10-20 hour) Diazepam ... Clonazepam ... Oxazepam"
findings.source: Whalen K. Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Pharmacology. 8th ed. Wolters Kluwer; 2023
findings.fix_hint: Short: midazolam, triazolam. Intermediate: alprazolam, lorazepam, oxazepam, temazepam. Long: diazepam, chlordiazepoxide, clonazepam, flurazepam.

findings.claim: The mechanism slide contradicts itself: it says BZs increase channel opening frequency, then that they 'do not affect the opening of the ion channel'.
findings.evidence: "benzodiazepines do not affect the opening of the ion channel"
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: BZs are positive allosteric modulators: no effect without GABA; with GABA they increase opening frequency.

findings.claim: Benzodiazepines are called 'very safe' with a toxic dose 1000-fold the therapeutic dose; combined with alcohol, opioids or other depressants they cause fatal respiratory depression (FDA boxed warning).
findings.evidence: "Benzodiazepines are very safe as toxic dose is 1000 fold the therapeutic dose."
findings.source: FDA boxed warning: benzodiazepines with opioids (2016); abuse and dependence (2020)
findings.fix_hint: Replace with: wide margin when taken alone, but combined with alcohol, opioids or other CNS depressants they can cause fatal respiratory depression; elderly: falls and confusion.

findings.claim: Flumazenil is an antagonist at the benzodiazepine site, not a GABA receptor antagonist.
findings.evidence: "is a GABA receptor antagonist"
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Competitive antagonist at the BZ site of the GABA-A receptor; short half-life, re-sedation possible.

findings.claim: Buspirone acts as a 5-HT1A partial agonist; the 5-HT2A attribution is wrong.
findings.evidence: "The actions of buspirone appear to be mediated by serotonin (5-HT1A) and (5-HT2A) receptors"
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: 5-HT1A partial agonist (some D2 affinity); onset 1-2 weeks or more.

findings.claim: Barbiturates are anticonvulsants; it is their withdrawal that lowers the seizure threshold.
findings.evidence: "Barbiturates ... can lower the seizure threshold."
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Say 'abrupt withdrawal can precipitate seizures'.

findings.claim: The barbiturate mechanism omits increased duration of chloride-channel opening and direct GABA-mimetic action at high doses, which explains their lower safety margin.
findings.evidence: "Allosteric modulation of GABA receptor ... action similar to BZ action"
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Contrast: BZs raise frequency; barbiturates raise duration and can open the channel without GABA.

findings.claim: Doxepin is a tricyclic antidepressant; its hypnotic effect at low dose is from H1 antagonism, not an SNRI mechanism.
findings.evidence: "Doxepin an older tricyclic agent with SNRI mechanisms"
findings.source: Whalen K. Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Pharmacology. 8th ed. Wolters Kluwer; 2023
findings.fix_hint: Low-dose doxepin (3-6 mg): selective H1 antagonism for sleep maintenance.

findings.claim: Inhaled-anaesthetic pharmacokinetics are absent: MAC, blood:gas partition coefficient and speed of induction/recovery are not taught.
findings.evidence: "Classification of general anesthetics: I. Inhalation agents ..."
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Add MAC (potency) and blood:gas solubility (speed) with a comparison table for N2O, sevoflurane, desflurane, isoflurane.

findings.claim: Malignant hyperthermia is said to occur when anaesthetics are used 'with' succinylcholine; either trigger alone can cause it.
findings.evidence: "may occur when anesthetics are used with NMBs like succinylcholine"
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Triggered by volatile anaesthetics and/or succinylcholine in susceptible (RYR1) patients.

findings.claim: Etomidate is listed but not described; its adrenal suppression and haemodynamic stability are key selection points.
findings.evidence: "Propofol – thiopental – etomidate – ketamine – midazolam"
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Add etomidate: haemodynamically stable induction; adrenal suppression, myoclonus, PONV.

findings.claim: Ketamine 'does not affect respiration' overstates; it causes minimal respiratory depression and preserves airway reflexes, but increases secretions.
findings.evidence: "Does not affect respiration."
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Minimal respiratory depression; bronchodilator; increases secretions.

findings.claim: The endoscopy MCQ key says D (sevoflurane) but the rationale explains midazolam (C).
findings.evidence: "Correct answer = D. Midazolam is used as a sole agent"
findings.source: internal contradiction
findings.fix_hint: Correct key: C.

findings.claim: Amides are labelled 'topical local anesthetics for the eyes'; the eye agents are esters/amides such as tetracaine and proxymetacaine; amides are mainly injected.
findings.evidence: "Amides: (topical local anesthetics for the eyes)."
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Remove the label; list ophthalmic agents separately.

findings.claim: Local anaesthetic systemic toxicity lacks seizures, bupivacaine cardiotoxicity, maximum doses and the 20% lipid emulsion treatment.
findings.evidence: "Adverse effects of local anesthetics due to over dose or inadvertent injection ..."
findings.source: AAGBI/ASRA LAST guideline (2020)
findings.fix_hint: Add LAST: CNS excitation then depression, arrhythmia/arrest (bupivacaine), max doses with/without adrenaline, 20% lipid emulsion.

findings.claim: The adrenaline statement gives no cautions: severely impaired peripheral circulation, and combination with cocaine or other potent sympathomimetics.
findings.evidence: "added to as epinephrine a vasoconstrictor"
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Add Caution: adrenaline-containing solutions are acceptable for most selected digital blocks; avoid or use specialist caution with severely impaired circulation, and avoid with cocaine or other potent sympathomimetics.

findings.claim: The general-anaesthesia endoscopy MCQ is repeated at the end of the local-anaesthetics chapter.
findings.evidence: Lines 3168-3187 repeat at 3333-3352
findings.source: editorial
findings.fix_hint: Remove the duplicate.

findings.claim: The source is nine slide decks: fragmented bullets, no learning objectives, no recap of prerequisites, no key takeaways, and teacher prompts ('4 minutes', 'the slides mention') mixed with student text.
findings.evidence: "Here is where your presentation begins"; "Case Study Deep Dive: Mr. S (4 minutes)"
findings.source: brief.goal; instructional-designer
findings.fix_hint: Rewrite into continuous chapters with objectives, Quick Recap, core sections, boxes, takeaways and assessment.

findings.claim: Spelling errors are frequent (seizuers, epilpsey, Benzodiazpeines, Barbiutates, hyperclosterolima, torsadogenic durgs).
findings.evidence: "is a disease charactraized by recurrent episodes of seizuers"
findings.source: editorial
findings.fix_hint: Copy-edit to en-GB.

findings.claim: Section numbering disagrees with the schedule (Depression numbered 05 before Epilepsy 04; two sections numbered 03 in the anxiolytics deck).
findings.evidence: "05 Depression" ... "04 epilepsy"
findings.source: brief.size.restructuring_note
findings.fix_hint: Use the approved chapter order.

findings.claim: Nineteen 'Brands' slides are package photographs only; the brand names are not in the text and product photos cannot be reproduced.
findings.evidence: "Brands" (19 slides with no text)
findings.fix_hint: Transcribe brand names into a 'Brands in Egypt' table per chapter; verify against the EDA list.

findings.claim: Assessment is uneven: 0-4 MCQs per chapter (none for skeletal muscle relaxants), five options (A-E) instead of four, and some rationales lack the answer letter.
findings.evidence: "Cases" slides; SMR has one case and no MCQ
findings.source: brief.assessment (10 MCQs A-D + 2-3 cases per chapter)
findings.fix_hint: Write 10 four-option MCQs and 2-3 clinical cases per chapter with rationales.

findings.claim: The source cites no references at all.
findings.evidence: No reference list in any deck
findings.source: brief.references
findings.fix_hint: Add a Vancouver reference list per chapter (core textbooks and current guidelines).

findings.claim: Across chapters, therapeutic choice is rarely justified by guideline or patient factors (Parkinson's initial therapy, epilepsy by seizure type, insomnia and GAD algorithms are thin or absent).
findings.evidence: "Treatment of Parkinson's disease will focus on ..."
findings.source: NICE NG71, NG217, NG222; APA schizophrenia guideline 2020
findings.fix_hint: Add a 'Choosing a drug' table per chapter.

findings.claim: Cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine are presented as slowing disease progression; they are symptomatic treatments with modest, temporary benefit and do not modify the disease course (repeated at lines 101-104 and 196-228).
findings.evidence: "medication only serves to slow the progression of disease"
findings.source: NICE NG97 (2018); Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Say 'may give modest temporary benefit in cognition or function'; contrast with anti-amyloid antibodies for eligible early disease.

findings.claim: SSRI sexual dysfunction is said to disappear after two weeks; nausea often settles, but sexual dysfunction commonly persists and must be reviewed.
findings.evidence: "GIT disturbance ... and erectile dysfunctions are the most common side effects of SSRI and they disappear after 2 weeks"
findings.source: NICE NG222 (2022); Taylor D et al. The Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines. 15th ed. 2025
findings.fix_hint: Separate early transient effects (nausea) from persistent ones (sexual dysfunction) and give management options.

findings.claim: Amantadine is said to potentiate dopamine reuptake; it increases release, inhibits reuptake and antagonises NMDA receptors (useful for levodopa-induced dyskinesia).
findings.evidence: "it may potentiate dopamine synthesis ,release and reuptake"
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Replace with release, reuptake inhibition and NMDA antagonism; note use in dyskinesia.

findings.claim: Loss of consciousness is said to be constant in all generalised seizures; awareness can be preserved in myoclonic seizures.
findings.evidence: "Loss of consciousness is constant with all three types of generalized seizures."
findings.source: Fisher RS et al. Operational classification of seizure types (ILAE). Epilepsia. 2017;58(4):522-530
findings.fix_hint: Describe awareness per seizure type (absence, tonic-clonic, myoclonic).

findings.claim: Vecuronium is said to form inactive metabolites; its 3-desacetyl metabolite is active and can accumulate.
findings.evidence: "vecuronium is hepatically metabolized to inactive metabolites"
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Mention the active 3-desacetyl metabolite and prolonged block in organ dysfunction.

findings.claim: Benzodiazepine indications mislead: OCD is listed as a routine indication, anticonvulsant use is 'no longer accepted', and diazepam is the only status-epilepticus choice; IV lorazepam or buccal/IM midazolam are preferred by setting and clobazam/clonazepam keep selected roles.
findings.evidence: "The use of BZ in treatment of epilepsy is no longer accepted" / "Diazepam is the drug of choice in terminating status epilepticus."
findings.source: NICE NG217 (2022); Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Remove OCD; separate rescue/status use (route-dependent choices) from maintenance use.

findings.claim: Z-drugs are said to show few withdrawal effects and little tolerance; they can cause dependence, withdrawal, next-day impairment and complex sleep behaviours (FDA boxed warning).
findings.evidence: "They show few withdrawal effects, exhibits minimal rebound insomnia, and little tolerance occurs"
findings.source: FDA Drug Safety Communication: boxed warning for complex sleep behaviours (2019)
findings.fix_hint: Add duration limits, dependence counselling, driving caution and the boxed warning.

findings.claim: Ketamine is called generally preferred in paediatrics and the MCQ keys it without a scenario; induction-agent choice depends on haemodynamics, airway, procedure and need for analgesia.
findings.evidence: "The adverse effects are less marked in children making it preferred in pediatrics."
findings.source: Gropper MA, ed. Miller's Anesthesia. 10th ed. Elsevier; 2024; Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Teach patient-specific selection; rewrite the MCQ around a haemodynamically unstable child needing painful procedural sedation.

findings.claim: The schizophrenia case answer switches to risperidone for involuntary movements without identifying the movement disorder; risperidone has dose-related EPS and anticholinergics can worsen tardive dyskinesia.
findings.evidence: "He had developed Extrapyramidal side effects, Which can be avoided by shifting to Atypical anti psychotic drugs (Risperidone)"
findings.source: Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines 15th ed.; APA Practice Guideline for Schizophrenia (2020)
findings.fix_hint: Identify the EPS type and timing, then give subtype-specific management.

findings.claim: Benzodiazepines in epilepsy are limited to status and febrile seizures; clobazam and clonazepam have maintenance roles in selected epilepsies.
findings.evidence: "Benzodiazipens. (limited to status epileptics I.V only and febrile sezuires I.V or rectal suppositories)"
findings.source: NICE NG217 (2022)
findings.fix_hint: Add clobazam/clonazepam as adjuncts.

findings.claim: Pancuronium is said to be eliminated renally unchanged; it is mainly renal but partly hepatic, with an active 3-hydroxy metabolite.
findings.evidence: "pancuronium is eliminated renally unchanged"
findings.source: Katzung BG, Vanderah TW. Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. 16th ed. McGraw Hill; 2024
findings.fix_hint: Say 'mainly renal excretion; avoid in renal failure'.
